Classify matches only as matched, unmatched, or unverified; unknown does not mean unmatched. Group by the stable platform identity returned by each platform, count each stable identity on a platform once, preserve every source and real provenance, and do not merge same-named accounts across platforms. Platform details follow the live contract: for example, YouTube's stable channel ID is its stable identity, so deduplicate only by platform + stable ID. The same connection and read depth are used only to reuse equivalent reads; pass depth: light or full when needed, with light intentionally omitting comments. Reuse equivalent requests with the same platform, connection, operation/schema revision, native arguments, depth, and cursor; do not resend because of call_id, display name, shape, or presentation reference. Start with evidence already returned by search. Before each supplementary read, state which fact is missing from the search results and which value would change the match or tier. Make one targeted supplementary read only when quality or geographic evidence is missing and could change the current decision; mark unknown and stop when the same gap remains unverifiable. When recent publication or content evidence already exists, do not get every channel again for review. Do not require new fields or unrelated quality due diligence; do not pre-read profile solely for a later save, and do not mechanically supplement same-tier candidates to make profiles more complete or split a tier. This workflow guide is the sole source for the scoring rubric: choose the tier first, then use the fixed score: excellent 95, good 85, medium 70, low 40. Excellent means a clear match with direct concrete evidence and a distinctive advantage relevant to this task. Good means a clear match with enough existing content evidence to support recommendation and no observed significant relevant weakness. Medium means the candidate meets the selection requirement but visible evidence has a recommendation limitation to explain. Low means the candidate may still meet the selection requirement but has a specific, citable, significant recommendation weakness; do not assign low only because of follower count or missing fields. Only when the user explicitly provides a minimum tier does the tier become an eligibility gate; otherwise matches may be delivered across tiers. Each per-candidate assessment must state its own concrete facts, relation to the requirement, and actual limitations; do not re-verify candidates in the same tier. Do not add follower, geographic, short-form-content, originality, or commercial-collaboration gates, and do not lower a tier automatically because a field is missing. Stop searching after reaching the matching target. If the target is not met, process candidates already obtained first, then continue within the originally approved scope under the same conditions using the actual cursor returned; do not fetch the first page again, change conditions, expand authority, or hide the actual gap. Complete search, matching, and per-candidate assessment after the search plan is confirmed. When delivering the candidate list, prepare one review using the existing candidate batch save flow: this is the prepare stage of onecrew.creator.candidate.batch.save, not a new operation. Use the live schema to call onecrew.creator.candidate.batch.save with candidates <=50 and explicit default intent add_new; use save_or_update only when the user explicitly requests an update. Submit the real target, connection, provenance, numeric score, and per-candidate assessment. The owner obtains fresh platform data during prepare; when search evidence is sufficient, do not issue an independent profile/channel get just because of saving. Use the owner's summary to explain eligible_new, eligible_update, existing_skipped, duplicate_skipped, identity_pending, contact_conflict, and failed; count only eligible_new toward the new-candidate target. Do not accept Agent profiles or caches. Preparation does not write Creator and does not auto-confirm. Present the returned result_ref, wait for the user to confirm consumption of the same immutable preparation, then read back the real result. The default delivery is a candidate review card. A pure Markdown list is not the default completion; only when the user explicitly requests plain text or no card, the user disallows additional preparation reads, or actual capability is blocked, explain the change and deliver that instead; do not silently trigger a write.
